answer: A V12 input computed from one measured and one assumed value is a derived value, and it carries the status of its weakest input: assumed, not measured. The calibration page defines derived as "a value computed from other inputs by a stated formula" and states that "a derived value inherits the weakest status of its inputs"; since measured is the stronger status of the pair, the computed parameter is labeled assumed (it cannot claim a measured source). That status is recorded per parameter in the model contract, so the label sticks to the parameter, not to the intermediate arithmetic. What can change it: only new evidence. A parameter can change status only with new evidence - in practice a real measurement of the previously assumed input (or an independent measurement of the computed quantity itself) that satisfies the measured definition: a named source plus a measurement method, sample size and period; the contract validator requires an evidence status of measured to be backed by a source and a measurement record. The same inheritance rule means the derived value's inherited status rises only when its weakest input is measured. Things that do not change it: repeating the assumed value in a decision record (explicitly stated not to make it measured), relabeling it, adding precision, or re-running the model. A scenario override that changes a parameter without updating the calibration note instead makes the evidence status ambiguous. Until a measurement exists, the model stays uncalibrated and any decision leaning on the computed value stays conditional or returns insufficient evidence, with the missing measurement and a review trigger named.
